tagline: Hosts, clusters, and databases in one window
summary: The sidebar is Hosts, Kubernetes, and Databases. The title-bar AI follows whichever one is open, and each object keeps its own chat. Home is the welcome page. Changes wait for approval, and STOP is always there.
feature.hosts.title: Hosts
feature.hosts.desc: Multi-tab SSH. The host icon opens that machine’s desktop: files, processes, a browser on the host network, and a terminal.
feature.kubernetes.title: Kubernetes
feature.kubernetes.desc: Add a cluster, or bind kubectl on a host you already connected. Browse workloads, YAML, logs, and Helm. One cluster, one chat.
feature.databases.title: Databases
feature.databases.desc: Connect directly to PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, SQL Server, Oracle, MongoDB, and Redis. One service, one tab, one chat. Table tabs show the database and schema.
feature.ai.title: AI
feature.ai.desc: Built-in models, or Cursor, Codex, and Claude Code already signed in on this machine. Ask in plain language about the host, cluster, or database that is open. Home does not show a chat.
feature.safety.title: Approval and STOP
feature.safety.desc: Read-only work can run on its own. Changes wait for your approval. STOP ends the run, including external agents.
step.hosts.text: Connect a Linux host from the Hosts sidebar, or open its desktop.
step.kubernetes.text: Switch to Kubernetes and add a cluster.
step.databases.text: Switch to Databases and add a connection. After you run your own SQL, the restore icon returns the table’s default data.
